analysis:
The PR modifies docs/architecture/inference.md only. The supplied units are base_text excerpts (base lines 4003-4494) and do not overlap the changed ranges, which are base 3, 126, 3045, 3096, 4478, 4860-4870. Head ranges include added text at 4483-4485 and 4505-4538 (apparently Gemma batch decode and pipeline lanes documentation) and 4901-4927. The base excerpt shows the surrounding Gemma batch decode arithmetic section ending at base line 4494. The only visible patch hunks (first three) change the update date, add Gemma 4 pipeline default-width wording, and reference an anchor.

No code, key handling, attestation, authorization, or wire-protocol behavior changes in the visible material. This is documentation drift, not a control change. The base excerpts I reviewed describe pre-existing behavior: sealed all-sum (AES-256-GCM) on the keyed JACCL data plane, encrypted SSD prefix records scoped per tenant partition, the rule that an oversized boundary requires an encrypted data plane with no raw fallback, and load-agreement binding that fails closed on mismatch. These are consistent with T-041 (prefix-cache and at-rest posture) and the TB-002/TB-007 assumptions. I found no statements that weaken these. The excerpt documents the 'record' encodings as lossy-by-contract with native mode exact, which matches the existing accepted posture.

Limits: the patch excerpt is truncated, so the head-side additions at 4505-4538 and 4901-4927 were not visible. If those lines describe a new default lane width for Gemma 4 serial-prefill pipelines, the next pass should check that the described default does not claim qualification, does not change admission or LOAD safeguards, and does not alter prefix-cache tenant scoping or SSD-tier claims in T-041. I raise no finding and set needs_deeper_review=false because the visible changes are doc-only; the unseen hunks are a coverage limit rather than evidence of risk.
